restrictions: The witness is the ordinary collision of the two distinct 128-byte messages in certificates/manifest.json under standard-IV SHA-256 reduced to steps 0 through 30, with FIPS padding and all 256 digest bits.

time_log2 40.2 and preprocessing_log2 40.2 are the same ceiling. The explicit sum in proof.md is 1098652007288.16 target compressions, whose base-2 logarithm is 39.99887163061176, strictly below 2^40.2.
Every search trial is charged at 501 primitive 32-bit operations divided by 2140, including failed sparse-table runs and 120 seconds of unlogged overshoot on the killed fast run.
The z3 term is the hardware ceiling in H-Z3-HARDWARE-CEILING. It is included in the sum. It is not an instruction trace.
Expected time is not used. The yield search final counter includes sibling-thread work after the collision index.
This package claims no full SHA-256 collision and no 32-round collision.

heuristics.statement: All local z3 5.1.0 attempts that produced or failed to produce the starting solution are charged at 16 cores * 6e9 cycles/s * 8 32-bit operations/cycle * 1200 seconds / 2140 = 430654205607.4766 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The one-time starting-solution search for the witness in proof.md, including timed-out attempts on the same characteristic.
heuristics.extrapolation: z3 emits no collision-frontier-v5 trace. The bound uses the whole 16-core machine for 1200 seconds even though the process was single-threaded and the successful bit-blast returned before its 150-second timeout. Eight operations per cycle is above a sustained integer throughput for this CPU. A smaller trace would only lower the claim.
heuristics.limitations: The bound is not a retired-instruction receipt. If a reviewer shows that the charged attempts exceeded 16*6e9*8*1200 primitive 32-bit operations, the ceiling is invalid. Crossing 2^40.2 total units invalidates the score.
